topics.title: Introduction & Employer-Employee Relationship
explain: Income is taxable under 'Salaries' only when an employer-employee relationship exists between payer and payee.
Remuneration received by a director who is an employee is salary, but partner's salary from a firm is business income.
Salaries from full-time or part-time employment across single or multiple employers are clubbed together.
Waiver or forgoing of salary after it accrues is an application of income and remains fully taxable.
Salary earned for services rendered in India is deemed to accrue in India even if paid abroad.

flow.title: Taxability based on Payer-Payee Relationship
steps: Check payer payee agreement
Determine if master servant relation exists
If employer employee relation exists
Tax income under head Salaries
If no employer employee relation
Tax under Business or Other Sources

topics.example: Sujata works as an actress employed by Chopra Films for a fixed monthly salary; her income is taxed under Salaries even if external producers pay Chopra Films.
remember: Partner's salary from a firm is taxed under PGBP, not Salaries
Remuneration to MPs or MLAs is taxed under Income from Other Sources
mistakes: Assuming part-time employment salary is not chargeable under the head Salaries

quiz.q: How is salary paid to a partner by a partnership firm taxed under the Income-tax Act?
o: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
quiz.why: A partner is an owner, not an employee, so partner's salary is treated as appropriation of profits under PGBP.

quiz.q: Under which head is the remuneration received by a Member of Parliament taxable?
o: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
quiz.why: An MP is not a government employee, so no employer-employee relationship exists.

topics.title: Basis of Charge for Salary Income
explain: Salary is chargeable to tax on 'due' basis or 'receipt' basis, whichever is earlier.
Advance salary received in any tax year is taxed in the year of receipt and not taxed again when due.
Advance against salary is an adjustable loan from the employer and is not taxed as salary.
Arrears of salary are taxed in the year of receipt if they were not assessed on due basis earlier.

flow.title: Evaluating Basis of Charge
steps: Identify due date of salary
Identify actual date of receipt
Compare due date and receipt date
Select earlier of the two dates
Charge salary in that tax year

topics.example: An employee receives salary for April 2027 in advance during March 2027; it gets taxed in the tax year 2026-27 on receipt basis.
remember: Advance salary is taxable on receipt basis
Advance against salary is a loan and not taxable as salary
mistakes: Confusing advance salary (taxable income) with advance against salary (non-taxable loan)

quiz.q: What is the basis of charge for salary income under Section 15?
o: Due or receipt basis, whichever is earlier
Due or receipt basis, whichever is later
quiz.why: Section 15 clearly provides that salary is taxed on due or receipt basis, whichever occurs earlier.

quiz.q: How is an advance against salary treated for income tax purposes?
o: Treated as a loan and not taxed
Taxed under Income from Other Sources
quiz.why: Advance against salary is a loan repayable/adjustable in instalments, so it cannot be taxed as salary.

topics.title: Definition and Components of Salary
explain: Section 16 gives an inclusive definition of salary covering monetary and non-monetary items.
Salary includes basic wages, annuity, pension, gratuity, fees, commission, and taxable perquisites.
Encashment of unavailed leave and profits in lieu of salary form part of taxable salary.
Annual accretion to RPF above specified limits and employer's NPS contributions are included.

flow.title: Computation of Gross Salary Components
steps: Aggregate basic pay and wages
Add taxable allowances and bonus
Add taxable perquisites and benefits
Add retirement benefit payouts
Sum up to arrive at Gross Salary

topics.example: Basic pay of ₹40,000 p.m., monthly commission, dearness allowance, and rent-free house value are added together under Section 16.
remember: The definition under Section 16 is inclusive, not exhaustive
Includes both cash payments and non-cash perquisites
mistakes: Excluding non-monetary facilities while computing salary under Section 16

quiz.q: Which of the following describes the definition of salary under Section 16?
quiz.why: Section 16 provides an inclusive definition that encompasses monetary pay as well as perquisites and retirement benefits.

quiz.q: Are non-monetary perquisites included in the definition of salary under Section 16?
o: No, only monetary payments are included
quiz.why: Section 16 includes both monetary payments and non-monetary perquisites in the definition of salary.

topics.title: Taxability of Allowances
explain: Allowances are fixed monetary payments given to employees to meet specific expenses.
Dearness Allowance, City Compensatory Allowance, Overtime, and Entertainment Allowance are fully taxable.
HRA is exempt under the optional tax regime up to the least of: actual HRA, rent paid minus 10% salary, or 50%/40% of salary.
Under the default tax regime u/s 202(1), HRA and special personal allowances are fully taxable without exemption.

flow.title: HRA Exemption Evaluation (Optional Regime)
steps: Check if assessee pays house rent
Calculate actual HRA received
Calculate rent paid minus 10% salary
Calculate 50% or 40% of salary
Exempt the least of three amounts

topics.example: An employee in Delhi paying rent higher than 10% of salary gets HRA exemption equal to the lowest of actual HRA, excess rent paid, or 50% of salary under optional regime.
remember: Metro cities for 50% HRA limit: Mumbai, Kolkata, Delhi, Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad
HRA exemption is NOT available under default tax regime u/s 202(1)
mistakes: Claiming HRA or Children Education Allowance exemption while paying tax under default tax regime

quiz.q: What percentage of salary is taken for HRA exemption limit in non-metro cities?
quiz.why: For accommodation located in cities other than specified metro cities, the salary limit for HRA is 40%.

quiz.q: Is House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption available under the default tax regime u/s 202(1)?
quiz.why: HRA exemption is allowed only if the employee opts out of the default tax regime u/s 202(4).

topics.title: Taxability of Pension & Annuity
explain: Uncommuted periodic pension is fully taxable for both government and non-government employees.
Commuted pension lump sum is fully deductible u/s 19(1) for Government employees, defence staff, and judges.
For non-Government employees receiving gratuity, 1/3rd of full commuted value of pension is deductible u/s 19(1).
For non-Government employees not receiving gratuity, 1/2 of full commuted value of pension is deductible u/s 19(1).

flow.title: Commuted Pension Deduction Process
steps: Check if employee is Government employee
If Govt: Full commuted amount deductible
If Non-Govt: Check receipt of gratuity
If Gratuity received: Deduct 1/3 total commuted value
If No Gratuity: Deduct 1/2 total commuted value

topics.example: A private employee commutes 60% pension for ₹3,00,000 and receives gratuity; total value is ₹5,00,000, so 1/3rd (₹1,66,667) is deductible.
remember: Uncommuted pension is ALWAYS fully taxable for everyone
Commuted pension deduction u/s 19(1) is available under BOTH tax regimes
mistakes: Applying commuted pension deduction formulas to uncommuted periodic pension payments

quiz.q: How is uncommuted (periodic) pension treated for a private sector employee?
quiz.why: Uncommuted pension received periodically is fully taxable for all categories of employees.

quiz.q: What portion of commuted pension is deductible for a non-government employee who also receives gratuity?
quiz.why: If a non-government employee receives gratuity, deduction u/s 19(1) is restricted to 1/3rd of the full value of commuted pension.

topics.title: Taxability and Deduction of Gratuity
explain: Gratuity received during active service is fully taxable in the hands of all employees.
Gratuity received on retirement or death by Government employees is fully deductible u/s 19(1).
For non-Govt employees covered by Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, deduction is least of: ₹20 lakh, actual gratuity, or 15/26 x last salary x completed years.
For non-Govt employees not covered, deduction is least of: ₹20 lakh, actual gratuity, or 1/2 x avg 10 months salary x completed years.

flow.title: Gratuity Deduction Computation
steps: Check timing of gratuity receipt
If during service: Fully taxable
If on retirement: Check employer category
Govt employee: Entire amount deductible
Non-Govt: Apply least of 3 statutory limits

topics.example: A private employee covered under Gratuity Act with 27 years service gets ₹15 lakh; deduction is least of ₹20L, ₹15L, or 15/26 x salary x 27.
remember: Maximum statutory limit for gratuity deduction is ₹20 Lakhs
Under Payment of Gratuity Act, month is taken as 26 days and fraction > 6 months is rounded up
mistakes: Rounding up part of year for employees NOT covered under the Payment of Gratuity Act

quiz.q: What is the maximum statutory deduction limit for gratuity under Section 19(1)?
quiz.why: The maximum statutory limit for gratuity deduction for non-government employees is ₹20,00,000.

quiz.q: How many days in a month are taken for salary calculation under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972?
quiz.why: For employees covered under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the number of days in a month is fixed at 26.

topics.title: Leave Encashment / Leave Salary
explain: Leave salary received during the period of service is fully taxable for all employees.
Leave encashment on retirement received by Government employees is fully deductible u/s 19(1).
For non-Govt employees on retirement, deduction is least of: ₹25 lakh, actual amount, 10 months' avg salary, or cash equivalent of unavailed leave.
Unavailed leave calculation is restricted to a maximum entitlement of 30 days per year of actual service.

flow.title: Leave Encashment Deduction Steps
steps: Check timing of receipt
If during service: Fully taxable
If on retirement: Check Govt status
If Govt: Fully deductible
If Non-Govt: Calculate 4 prescribed limits
Deduct least of the four limits

topics.example: A retiring private employee receives ₹5,00,000 leave salary; deduction is least of ₹25L, ₹5L, 10 months' average salary, and cash value of leave balance.
remember: Maximum lifetime limit for leave encashment deduction is ₹25 Lakhs
Leave entitlement for calculation cannot exceed 30 days per completed year
mistakes: Taking leave entitlement higher than 30 days per year when calculating unavailed leave standing at credit

quiz.q: What is the lifetime statutory limit for leave encashment deduction for non-government employees?
quiz.why: The Central Government has specified ₹25,00,000 as the maximum lifetime deduction limit for leave salary encashment.

quiz.q: How is leave encashment received during active service taxed?
quiz.why: Leave encashment received during employment is fully taxable as salary for both government and non-government employees.

topics.title: Provident Funds, NPS & Agniveer Corpus Fund
explain: Accumulated balance from Recognised Provident Fund (RPF) on retirement is exempt if service is at least 5 years.
Interest on employee's PF contribution exceeding ₹2.5 lakh p.a. (₹5 lakh if no employer contribution) is taxable as per Rule 277.
Employer contribution to RPF, NPS, and Superannuation Fund exceeding ₹7.5 lakh p.a. in aggregate is taxable as perquisite u/s 17(1)(h).
Annual accretion (interest/dividend) on such excess employer contribution is taxable u/s 17(1)(i).
Employer contribution to NPS (Section 124) and Agniveer Corpus Fund (Section 125) is included in salary and deductible under Chapter VI-A.

flow.title: Taxing Excess Employer Contribution to PF/NPS
steps: Sum employer contribution to RPF NPS Superannuation
Check if aggregate exceeds ₹7,50,000
Tax excess over ₹7,50,000 u/s 17(1)(h)
Compute annual accretion on excess amount
Tax annual accretion u/s 17(1)(i)

topics.example: If employer contributes ₹8,00,000 to NPS, ₹50,000 excess is taxed as a perquisite, and interest on that excess is taxed under Rule 16.
remember: Combined employer contribution cap for RPF, NPS, and Superannuation Fund is ₹7.5 Lakhs
Employee PF interest threshold: ₹2.5L (with employer contribution) or ₹5L (without employer contribution)
mistakes: Forgetting to compute taxable interest accretion u/s 17(1)(i) when employer contribution exceeds ₹7.5 lakhs

quiz.q: What is the combined annual threshold limit for employer's contribution to RPF, NPS, and Superannuation Fund beyond which it is taxed as perquisite?
quiz.why: Under Section 17(1)(h), aggregate employer contribution to RPF, NPS, and superannuation fund in excess of ₹7,50,000 is taxable as perquisite.

quiz.q: What is the employee contribution threshold in RPF beyond which interest becomes taxable (where employer also contributes)?
quiz.why: Interest on employee contribution exceeding ₹2,50,000 p.a. is taxable when employer also contributes to the fund.

topics.title: Perquisites Valuation - Accommodation & Sweat Equity
explain: Rent-free accommodation (RFA) provided by Government is valued at licence fee fixed by Govt minus rent paid.
RFA owned by non-Govt employer: 10% of salary (population > 40L), 7.5% (population 15L-40L), or 5% (other areas), minus rent paid.
RFA leased by employer: Lower of actual lease rent or 10% of salary, minus rent paid by employee.
Furnished accommodation adds 10% p.a. of original cost of furniture (or actual hire charges) to unfurnished value.
Specified securities / Sweat equity shares: Perquisite value is Fair Market Value (FMV) on option exercise date minus amount recovered.

flow.title: Valuation of Non-Government Owned RFA
steps: Determine city population as per 2011 census
If > 40L: Take 10% of salary
If 15L to 40L: Take 7.5% of salary
If <= 15L: Take 5% of salary
Add 10% p.a. cost of owned furniture
Subtract rent actually paid by employee

topics.example: A company-owned flat in Mumbai (pop > 40L) provided to an employee: perquisite value is 10% of salary plus 10% p.a. cost of furniture minus rent recovered.
remember: Population > 40 lakhs: 10% of salary
Population 15L to 40L: 7.5% of salary
Other areas: 5% of salary
mistakes: Using WDV or market value of owned furniture instead of 10% p.a. of original cost

quiz.q: What percentage of salary is taken for valuation of unfurnished accommodation owned by employer in a city with population exceeding 40 lakhs?
quiz.why: As per Rule 15(2), in cities having population > 40 lakhs as per 2011 census, perquisite value is 10% of salary.

quiz.q: How is perquisite value calculated for sweat equity shares allotted to an employee?
o: FMV on exercise date minus amount paid by employee
quiz.why: Section 17(1)(d) specifies perquisite value as FMV of shares on the option exercise date minus amount paid/recovered.

topics.title: Perquisites Valuation - Motor Car & Other Benefits
explain: Employer car used partly for personal use (expenses met by employer): ₹5,000/pm (<=1.6L) or ₹7,000/pm (>1.6L) + ₹3,000/pm for chauffeur.
Car owned by employee reimbursed by employer (partly personal): Actual expenses minus ₹5,000/pm (<=1.6L) or ₹7,000/pm (>1.6L).
Interest-free/concessional loan: Interest computed at SBI rate on 1st April on max monthly balance minus interest paid (no perquisite if loan <= ₹2L or for specified diseases).
Free food/vouchers during office hours exempt up to ₹200 per meal.
Gift vouchers below ₹15,000 in aggregate during a tax year have nil perquisite value.
Transfer of movable assets: Actual cost minus normal wear & tear (Computers 50% WDV, Cars 20% WDV, Others 10% SLM) minus amount recovered.

flow.title: Motor Car Valuation (Employer Owned, Mixed Use, Expenses by Employer)
steps: Check engine cubic capacity
If <= 1.6 litres: Take ₹5,000 p.m.
If > 1.6 litres: Take ₹7,000 p.m.
Check if chauffeur provided
If chauffeur provided: Add ₹3,000 p.m.
Multiply total monthly value by months used

topics.example: An employer provides a 1.8L engine car with driver for mixed official and personal use; perquisite value is ₹7,000 + ₹3,000 = ₹10,000 per month.
remember: Car > 1.6L engine capacity: ₹7,000 p.m. + ₹3,000 p.m. chauffeur
Depreciation on asset transfer: Computer 50% WDV, Motor car 20% WDV, Other assets 10% SLM
mistakes: Applying 20% WDV depreciation rate to computers transferred to employees instead of 50% WDV

quiz.q: What is the monthly perquisite value for a car > 1.6 litres with chauffeur owned and maintained by employer for mixed use?
quiz.why: Perquisite value is ₹7,000 p.m. for engine > 1.6L plus ₹3,000 p.m. for chauffeur, totaling ₹10,000 p.m.

quiz.q: What rate of normal wear and tear depreciation is applied on transfer of computers to employees?
quiz.why: For computers and electronic items, normal wear and tear is calculated @ 50% on Written Down Value (WDV) method.

topics.title: Tax-Free Perquisites & Medical Facilities
explain: Medical treatment in employer's hospital, Government hospital, or approved hospital is a tax-free perquisite.
Health insurance premium paid or reimbursed by employer is fully tax-free.
Medical treatment abroad is exempt up to RBI limit; travel expenses abroad are exempt if Gross Total Income <= ₹8,00,000.
Leave Travel Concession (LTC) is exempt under Schedule III for 2 journeys in a 4-year block (only under optional tax regime).
Use of laptops, computers, telephone, and mobile phone bills reimbursed by employer are completely tax-free perquisites.

flow.title: Exemption Evaluation for Medical Treatment Abroad
steps: Check treatment and stay cost abroad
Exempt up to RBI permitted limit
Check travel cost abroad for patient and attendant
Check Gross Total Income before including travel expense
If GTI <= ₹8,00,000: Travel expense fully exempt
If GTI > ₹8,00,000: Travel expense fully taxable

topics.example: Employer pays ₹1,05,000 for employee's medical treatment abroad (RBI limit ₹2,50,000); entire amount is exempt from tax.
remember: LTC exemption is available ONLY under the optional tax regime
Foreign travel medical exemption requires GTI <= ₹8 Lakhs before adding travel expense
mistakes: Assuming medical allowance is exempt (medical allowance is fully taxable; only medical reimbursement has exemptions)

quiz.q: What is the Gross Total Income limit for claiming exemption on foreign travel expenses for medical treatment?
quiz.why: Rule 19 prescribes that travel expenses for medical treatment abroad are exempt if GTI (before adding travel expense) does not exceed ₹8,00,000.

quiz.q: How is fixed monthly medical allowance paid by an employer treated under Income-tax Law?
quiz.why: Fixed medical allowance is a fully taxable allowance; only reimbursement of actual medical expenses has specific exemptions.

topics.title: Profits in Lieu of Salary & Compensations
explain: Profits in lieu of salary include compensation for termination or modification of employment terms.
Payments under Keyman Insurance Policy or receipts before joining or after leaving job are taxable u/s 18.
Retrenchment compensation deduction u/s 19(1) is least of: actual received, ₹5,00,000, or 15 days' avg pay x completed service years.
Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) compensation deduction u/s 19(1) is least of: actual received, ₹5,00,000, or (3 x completed years x salary) or (balance months x salary).

flow.title: VRS Compensation Deduction Steps
steps: Check eligibility (10 yrs service or 40 yrs age)
Determine actual VRS compensation received
Take statutory cap of ₹5,00,000
Compute 3 x completed years x salary
Compute remaining months of service x salary
Deduct least of the above amounts u/s 19(1)

topics.example: An employee receives ₹7,00,000 on voluntary retirement after 30 years service with 6 years left; deduction is capped at statutory limit of ₹5,00,000.
remember: Maximum statutory limit for VRS and Retrenchment compensation deduction is ₹5,00,000
VRS deduction is allowed only once in lifetime
mistakes: Claiming VRS deduction u/s 19(1) when Section 157 tax relief has been claimed for the same

quiz.q: What is the maximum statutory monetary limit for retrenchment compensation deduction u/s 19(1)?
quiz.why: The Central Government notified maximum limit for retrenchment compensation deduction is ₹5,00,000.

quiz.q: How many times can an employee claim voluntary retirement compensation deduction in their lifetime?
quiz.why: Where deduction for voluntary retirement compensation has been allowed for any tax year, no deduction is allowed in any other tax year.

topics.title: Deductions from Salary & Relief u/s 157
explain: Standard deduction u/s 19(1): ₹75,000 (or salary, whichever is lower) under default regime u/s 202(1); ₹50,000 under optional tax regime.
Professional tax paid by employee is deductible u/s 19(1) ONLY under the optional tax regime (max levy ₹2,500/yr).
If employer pays professional tax, it is first added to salary as a perquisite and then deducted (under optional regime).
Relief u/s 157 is granted when salary received in arrears or advance results in tax being charged at a higher rate than normal.

flow.title: Deductions from Gross Salary
steps: Compute Gross Salary
Select tax regime
If Default Regime: Deduct standard deduction up to ₹75,000
If Optional Regime: Deduct standard deduction up to ₹50,000
Deduct professional tax paid (Optional regime only)
Arrive at Net Income under head Salaries

topics.example: Under default tax regime u/s 202(1), Gross Salary of ₹7,16,000 is reduced by Standard Deduction of ₹75,000, giving Net Salary of ₹6,41,000.
remember: Standard Deduction: ₹75,000 under default tax regime u/s 202(1)
Standard Deduction: ₹50,000 under optional tax regime
Professional tax deduction is NOT available under default regime
mistakes: Deducting professional tax while computing salary under the default tax regime

quiz.q: What is the maximum Standard Deduction allowed under the default tax regime u/s 202(1)?
quiz.why: Under Section 19(1) for default tax regime u/s 202(1), standard deduction is ₹75,000 or salary, whichever is lower.

quiz.q: Is professional tax paid by an employee deductible under the default tax regime u/s 202(1)?
o: No, deduction is not allowed under default tax regime
quiz.why: Deduction for professional tax u/s 19(1) is available only if the employee opts out of default regime u/s 202(4).
